Ways to avoid a scam

There's no fool-proof way to avoid a scam, but you can minimize your chances. Doing your research up-front is key. If you go to a legit site with reviews of providers, there's a better chance you'll get what you are asking for. Bait and switch aside, which can happen when you get to the spa, generally the reviews are reliable indicators of the quality of providers at a given place.

Things that you can do include:

  • Do your research - see above

  • Perform a reverse google image search on the provider - If she's on many sites in different cities, it's likely a fake picture and should be avoided

  • Search her phone number on Google - A search may reveal more information on your provider include listings on websites that may include reviews. You can also see if that number has been in use for a long time, or a short period.

  • If it's too good to be true, it likely is - Self explanatory

LE is pervasive and they love to bust spas for quality of life issues. It's difficult to completely avoid LE and getting caught is a risk inherent in mongering. However, there are a few things you can do to ease the risk a bit. If your spa is in a high trafficked area where parking is in short supply, this will increase that neighbors will complain. What should I be paying for service

The fee is comprised of the house fee and the tip. You may see it broken out as follows: $0.6/1.2. This means there was a $60 house fee and $120 paid as a tip to the provider. There is always a debate in the monger community what the proper "tip" is, so this is just a guideline. Obviously, the providers want as large a tip as possible and mongers generally want to pay less.

Generally, the higher quality service the more you'll be paying. There are spas in Chinatown-NYC that really "crank them out", or a high volume shop that might be $0.4/.4 for a half-hour. Then, there are higher quality places with showers, locker rooms, and even American girls for much, much more. There are many variables, but I've found the following is true:

You should always pay with cash even if the spa accepts credit card. You don't want the credit card transaction permanently on your record. Also, the spa will believe there is a greater likelihood you are LE especially if going there the first time.

  • Tips are more dynamic based on the level of service and the quality of the provider. A handjob is the lowest service, a blowjob is in the middle and "full service" (FS) is everything including intercourse. As you can imagine there are some extras.
